answer:
Review the licence’s scope, term, renewal mechanics, fees, audit/reporting duties, data-use limits, termination triggers, cure periods, transition assistance and post-termination obligations. Map the index provider’s discretion: methodology changes, correction policies, calculation/continuity commitments, and any rights to suspend or discontinue the index. Check whether failed renewal permits temporary continued use, a transition window, or an orderly liquidation—and whether those are express, conditional rights, not assumptions.

Trace naming dependencies across the fund’s legal name, ticker, prospectus/marketing materials, exchange listing and index-provider trademarks. Identify required rebranding, filing, shareholder, exchange or notice steps and who controls each; do not assume a universal notice period.

Assess affiliated-information provisions: whether the provider or an affiliate sponsors competing products, receives holdings or transaction data, can share it internally, and what confidentiality, information-barrier, conflict-management and record-retention safeguards apply. Confirm practical access to index data, constituent files and historical records needed for compliance, valuation and transition planning.
